I'm going to nitpick.

Tor provides anonymity, not privacy. All of one's traffic to the open internet is visible to the exit node.
Never thought of it that way. How are the two different?

Imagine a masked person on TV giving a speech. Everyone can hear what he says. Technically, he could be speaking in code so that only those in the know understand him, but that's optional.

That is what Tor is like. No one can identify the origin of network traffic, but the exit node PLUS the intended receiver and EVERY other router between the exit node and the recipient will see what is said.

Tor does not provide end-to-end encryption, it only anonymizes.

If one wishes to keep anyone except the intended recipient from reading that traffic, additional encryption is required and is totally possible to use on top of tor. SSL accomplishes this, SSL's own problems notwithstanding.
